elements.text: Reflection of water waves can be observed by placing various obstacles in the tray of the ripple tank. The depth of the water can also be varied by laying glass plates of different thicknesses in the tray. This allows the observation of waves travelling from one medium to another.
**Aim:** To observe the reflection of water waves in a ripple tank.
**Material:** Ripple tank, barriers of different shapes (straight barrier, wooden block, concave and convex barriers), and droppers

items.text: Assemble the ripple tank as illustrated in Figure 1.13.
Set up the barrier in the ripple tank as shown in Figure 1.14
Switch ON the motor to run the oscillating paddle that generates some waves in the ripple tank.
Put some water into a dropper.
Hold the dropper about \(2\,\mathrm{cm}\) above the water surface.
Let one drop of water fall at the middle of the ripple tank.
Observe how the water waves will be reflected after striking the barrier.

crop.description: Ripple tank with straight barrier at 45 degrees and incident wavefronts.

items.text: Draw the incident and the reflected wave patterns in steps 4 and 9.
Change the angle of the barrier and repeat steps 3-9. Observe any changes in the reflected waves.
Replace the rectangular barrier with a curved one (concave) as shown in Figure 1.15, and repeat steps 3-9.

crop.description: Ripple tank with concave curved barrier, direction arrow and incident wavefronts.

items.text: Replace the concave barrier with a convex one and repeat steps 3-9.
Observe any changes in the reflected waves.
